data.title: Robot Dog Leads Chinese Soldiers in Urban Combat Drills
data.description: The video, posted by military watcher Clash Archivist on July 26, shows a robot dog—likely based on the $2,800 Unitree Go2—entering a structure ahead of troops during practical combat training. These lightweight machines scout high-risk areas like doorways, clear obstacles, and provide fire support to cut human casualties, as China's state media has demonstrated in chemical defense and amphibious exercises. While the footage highlights China's robotics edge and sparks talk of vulnerabilities like hacking, it reflects a global shift where infantry teams up with AI companions rather than being replaced.
